Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has recalled how the outcome of the 2023 presidential election in Lagos caught his political camp off guard, describing the defeat of President Bola Tinubu in the state as being “blindsided”. Fashola spoke during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday night, while responding to a question about the possibility of another major electoral upset in the 2027 general election. The interviewer recalled that Tinubu, who had governed Lagos State for eight years, lost the state to the Labour Party’s Peter Obi in the 2023 presidential election, prompting speculation that a bigger surprise could happen in 2027. Responding, Fashola said he had described the outcome at the time as being blindsided, but argued that political parties should understand that electoral victories cannot be guaranteed in every part of the country. “Look, listen, I told you then, I think I recall the word I used was that we were blindsided in Lagos. I told you that. And, you know, our democracy is maturing,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The former governor, who served as Minister of Works and Housing under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, went on to compare electoral contests with football, arguing that teams sometimes keep visiting grounds where they have repeatedly failed to win. He referenced former President Goodluck Jonathan’s football analogy, describing it as a useful way of understanding the unpredictability of elections. “I heard President Jonathan in your intro speaking about how the analogy of a contest in an election and using football, and it’s a very brilliant analogy, if you ask me,” Fashola said. He explained that some football clubs repeatedly visit opponents’ grounds despite having a history of losing there, because they still believe they can win. And most times you can’t win everywhere. There are places where you have your ardent and fervent supporters. Your responsibility there is to ensure that you do enough to get them out to vote,” he said In the 2023 presidential election, Obi defeated Tinubu in Lagos, polling 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606, according to results reported by The PUNCH. Obi won nine of the state’s 20 local government areas, while Tinubu won the remaining 11. The result was particularly significant because Tinubu had governed Lagos between 1999 and 2007 and remained a major political figure in the state. The PUNCH had reported that the result marked a major upset in the state’s political landscape, with Obi defeating Tinubu despite the latter’s long-standing influence in Lagos politics. Tinubu, however, went on to win the overall presidential election, polling 8,794,726 votes to defeat Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party and Obi, who finished third nationally. The 2027 presidential election is scheduled for January 16, with Tinubu seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress Obi, who defeated Tinubu in Lagos in 2023, is now contesting under the Nigeria Democratic Congress while former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress. INEC has listed 18 candidates for the election. Okiki Adeduyite Okiki is a journalist with over seven years experience covering politics, foreign news, society, entertainment and the film industry.
